conviction_note: Mild negative. Monthly sales and the Kumamoto earthquake make an H1 miss against the company's own plan close to certain (H1 OP plan 14.2bn needed Q2 OP +15% y/y while Q2 group sales ran about -2%), and last year the company cut its full-year forecast 14% at the same print. But the miss is in public monthly data, September sales already rebounded (group total +3.0%, same-store +4.8%), the stock has given back 14% since 27 Aug and trades at 0.67x book. The release adds a forecast decision and an earthquake loss and nothing else, so p_up is 43 on abs 2.3 (-0.32). The findings sum to -0.6. The two numbers agree in sign and are on the same small scale.
bar: H1 (Mar-Aug) company plan: operating revenue 290.8bn, OP 14.2bn, ordinary profit 13.9bn, net profit 9.4bn, unchanged at Q1 (https://kabutan.jp/stock/finance?code=8273, https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260714/140120260713592221.pdf). Full-year plan OP 29.0bn / ordinary profit 28.4bn. Street full-year ordinary-profit consensus is 28,472m (kabuyoho, https://kabuyoho.jp/report?bcode=8273, data dated 2026-10-09), and QUICK OP consensus was 28,105m on 2026-07-13 (https://scouter.monex.co.jp/news/detail/8273_20260714_act_20260714_153021_2). So the street has NOT marked the full year below the plan. print_vs_bar_pct is my estimate of H1 OP against the 14.2bn H1 plan.

This name sells its prints.

findings.finding: A full-year cut is the likely addition. Q2 (Jun-Aug) group sales ran 97.4 / 99.9 / 96.0 percent of the prior year (total stores), and Kumamoto stores closed after the 28 July quake. Q1 OP was 6,860m, so the 14.2bn H1 OP plan needed Q2 OP of about 7,340m against 6,389m last year (+15%). H1 OP likely lands around 12-13bn. Last year's H1 print came with a full-year OP cut from 30.7bn to 26.4bn (-14%), and the street (ordinary-profit consensus 28.47bn) still sits on the plan.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-10-14: H1 print with a 14% full-year OP cut, next session -1.98% (Yahoo chart). 2024-08-28: a late forecast plus control issues, -7.84%. A held forecast has never been tested at an H1 in this record.
findings.why_not_priced: The H1 miss itself is priced: the monthly figures are public and the stock is down 14% from late August. What is not visible is the forecast decision. If the market already expected a cut, the published consensus would sit below the 28.4bn ordinary-profit plan; it sits at 28.47bn. A cut of 3-7% would therefore land below the published street number. Sized small because the print-day selling in this name has been about -2% even on a 14% cut, and because September's rebound gives management grounds to hold the forecast.
findings.independence: Last year's precedent comes from a different document, the 2025-10-14 revision notice (https://www.izumi.co.jp/ir/57f2f1592c8c886450306883fc2f9f00.pdf). The H1 plan and Q1 progress come from the Q1 短信 (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260714/140120260713592221.pdf). The quake disruption comes from the company's own TDnet notice (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260730/140120260730503007.pdf: 16 of 35 Kumamoto stores still closed on 30 July).

findings.finding: An earthquake extraordinary loss has not yet been disclosed. Izumi's two quake notices (29 and 30 July) say the earnings impact is 'under investigation' and nothing has followed. Peer イオン九州 already booked a 1,745m 災害による損失 in its Q2 for about 20 affected stores, with more to come in Q3. Izumi runs 35 Kumamoto stores, 6 of them excluded from the Jul/Aug same-store figures as damaged and 3 still excluded in September. A loss of the same order (roughly 2-4bn) against a 9.4bn H1 net-profit plan is likely in this release.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2025-04-14 FY print with a special-loss notice: -0.73% the next session. No earthquake loss in the 3-year tape.
findings.why_not_priced: The amount is unknown, and Izumi, unlike its peer, has not pre-announced one. Holders who read the イオン九州 notice will expect a loss, so only the size can surprise. If the market had sized it, a figure would appear in the consensus net profit, which still tracks the plan (QUICK NI 17.3bn against a 17.4bn plan). It is below operating income with no path to the guide beyond the net-profit line, so it is sized at a fraction of the same yen in OP. A quake loss is also a classic 悪材料出尽くし (bad news finally out) item.
findings.independence: Izumi's own quake notices (https://tdnet-pdf.kabutan.jp/20260729/140120260729501351.pdf). The monthly page footnote excluding 6 damaged stores in Jul/Aug and 3 in September (https://www.izumi.co.jp/ir/finance/monthly/). The peer's notice is a different issuer and a different document.

findings.finding: September monthly sales, published 2026-10-09, rebounded hard: group total 全店 103.0, 既存店 104.8; directly operated 既存店 102.1 with average spend 102.2, against a weak September 2025 base of 98.5. This is the first month of H2 and gives management a documented basis to hold the 29.0bn full-year OP plan, or to trim it less than last year.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose +0.43% on 10-09, the day of the September monthly, and +0.75% intraday on 10-13 against a Nikkei down 2.3% at 10:17 JST (kabutan).
findings.why_not_priced: Only one session has traded since the number came out (10-12 was a holiday), and the market reads a monthly figure only when management frames it in the outlook at the results. If it were already priced as a held guide, the stock would not still sit near its 6-month low at 0.67x book. Partly reconstruction demand, so sized small.
findings.independence: The 2025 base month comes from a different document, the 2025 monthly backnumber (https://www.izumi.co.jp/corp/ir/pdf/backnumber/2025.pdf: Sep-25 group total 98.5). It shares the monthly page with finding 1. The two are different months and are not double-counted: finding 1 rests on Jun-Aug, this one on September.

findings.finding: Shareholder returns are unlikely to surprise. The third mid-term plan (April 2026) sets a consolidated payout of 30% or more with progressive dividends and only 'flexible' buybacks, and states that growth investment takes priority over stronger returns despite PBR below 1. Past buybacks (April 2025, January 2026) were ToSTNeT-3 trades absorbing cross-shareholding sales, not market programmes. So the interim dividend of 15 yen should hold despite the earnings cut, and a large return announcement is improbable.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: 2026-01-13 Q3 print with a ToSTNeT-3 buyback (0.85% of shares): -0.49% the next session.
findings.why_not_priced: Priced: the policy is public. It is filed so that the item-2 check is on record. The progressive dividend floors the downside of a profit cut, and a cross-shareholding ToSTNeT buyback is possible but undocumented, hence the asymmetric range.
findings.independence: January 2026 buyback notice (https://www.izumi.co.jp/ir/f8a53ed72ff1efbf71bf214e841c4fa7.pdf), which gives the cross-shareholding rationale.

outside_window.finding: イオン九州 says further quake costs will be booked from Q3 onward. Izumi is likely to follow, so any residual quake loss and reconstruction-demand upside fall in H2 prints.

bar_hierarchy: Forecast revision: plausible-to-likely full-year cut (last year cut 14% at H1; this year an H1 miss is visible plus the quake), with consensus still on the plan; September's rebound is the case for a hold. Returns: progressive 30%+ payout, interim 15 yen expected held, no buyback programme expected. New-year guide: n/a (H1 print). baseline_tension: Mostly agrees with the run-up (-5% over 20 sessions, -14% from the August peak), so part of the negative is in the price, and it cuts slightly against the mildly positive priced lean (+0.13). The strongest positive the release could carry: a held 29.0bn full-year guide backed by September's +4.8% same-store sales (filed as +0.3), the progressive dividend held, an opportunistic ToSTNeT buyback (searched; nothing announced), and the quake loss read as bad news finally out. I looked for each.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a negative resting on public 月次 goes toward 50 unless the release adds a forecast cut): finding 1 trimmed from -0.8 to -0.6, because part of it rested on the visible Q2 miss. p_up moved from 40 to 43; it is not moved to 50 because a full-year cut is a plausible ADD here (last year's precedent, consensus still on plan).
Rule 2 (check the sign, look for the positive): strongest positives were written into baseline_tension and already filed as findings 3 and 4 in the draft; nothing further moved.
